# description: Standard deviation across distinct number_sets of the per-set yes rate; observed above null means sets differ more in overall endorsement (rule vs similarity sets) than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    s = pd.Series(r).groupby(df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()).mean()
    v = float(s.std(ddof=0)) if len(s) > 1 else 0.0
    return v if np.isfinite(v) else 0.0

results.name: common_divisor_rule_contrast
results.description: In size>=2 sets whose GCD is >=3 and not 10, yes rate for targets divisible by the GCD minus not divisible (distance>5 from examples); observed above null means the model under-produces multiples-rule generalisation beyond final-digit similarity.
results.code:
# name: common_divisor_rule_contrast
# description: In size>=2 sets whose GCD is >=3 and not 10, yes rate for targets divisible by the GCD minus not divisible (distance>5 from examples); observed above null means the model under-produces multiples-rule generalisation beyond final-digit similarity.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    g = np.gcd.reduce(Si, axis=1)
    sel = (n >= 2) & (g >= 3) & (g != 10) & (dist > 5)
    gg = np.where(g > 0, g, 1)
    div = (t % gg) == 0
    return m(sel & div) - m(sel & ~div)

results.name: parity_rule_contrast
results.description: In all-even sets of size>=2, yes rate for even minus odd targets at distance>10 from every example; observed above null means the model under-produces parity-rule generalisation.

# name: parity_rule_contrast
# description: In all-even sets of size>=2, yes rate for even minus odd targets at distance>10 from every example; observed above null means the model under-produces parity-rule generalisation.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)

# description: Correlation between trial_index and yes response; observed differing from null means response bias drifts over the session in a way the model does not capture.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    if np.std(ti) == 0 or np.std(r) == 0:
        return 0.0
    v = float(np.corrcoef(ti, r)[0, 1])
    return v if np.isfinite(v) else 0.0

results.name: power_of_two_contrast
results.description: In sets of size>=2 consisting only of powers of two, yes rate for unshown power-of-two targets minus other even targets (both not in set); observed above null means the model misses the powers-of-two rule.
results.code:
# name: power_of_two_contrast
# description: In sets of size>=2 consisting only of powers of two, yes rate for unshown power-of-two targets minus other even targets (both not in set); observed above null means the model misses the powers-of-two rule.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    p2 = np.isin(Si, [1,2,4,8,16,32,64]) | np.isnan(S)
    sp = (n >= 2) & np.all(p2, axis=1)
    tp = np.isin(t, [1,2,4,8,16,32,64])
    return m(sp & tp & (dist > 0)) - m(sp & ~tp & (t % 2 == 0) & (dist > 0))

results.name: interval_inside_vs_outside_near
results.description: In size>=2 sets, yes rate for unshown targets strictly inside [min,max] minus targets outside the range within 1-10 of nearest example; observed above null means the model under-weights interval/range-based generalisation.

# description: In size>=2 sets, yes rate for unshown targets strictly inside [min,max] minus targets outside the range within 1-10 of nearest example; observed above null means the model under-weights interval/range-based generalisation.
def test_statistic(df):
    S = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(S), axis=1)
    Si = np.nan_to_num(S, nan=0.0).astype(int)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(S - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    smin = np.nanmin(S, axis=1); smax = np.nanmax(S, axis=1)
    def m(mask):
        return float(np.mean(r[mask])) if np.sum(mask) > 0 else 0.0
    sel = n >= 2

    return m(sel & inside) - m(sel & outside)
